newsitem.title: USA: U.S. delays flight restrictions for Grand Canyon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. delays flight restrictions for Grand Canyon.

text.p: Disagreement among agencies has prompted the federal government to delay some of the more controversial parts of a plan to restrict tourist flights over the Grand Canyon National Park, The Washington Post reported in Friday editions.
The paper quoted a senior Interior Department official as saying that the government had held up until December a plan to double the size of a "no-flight zone" over the canyon.
In addition, a decision on new flight routes in the park was put on hold in a decision expected to be formally announced Friday by the Federal Aviation Administration, the newspaper said.
The delay was attributed to disagreements among federal agencies over how to reroute helicopters and aircraft that take thousands of visitors on park tours each year.
A new route proposed by the FAA has met criticism because activists charge it diverts the air traffic over another federal preserve, the Saddle Mountain Wilderness Area.

The Interior Department official said the delay was aimed at avoiding a rushed decision, and the agencies would work together to draw up new routes to go into effect early next year, the newspaper reported.
"The FAA has proposed a flight pattern that we feel, on reflection, doesn't achieve as much quiet as we would achieve if we went another way," the paper quoted the official as saying.
Other aspects of the flight-restriction plan, including a cap on the number of aircraft licensed to fly in the area, will go into effect in May.
